description: Develop a chromatography separation method from analyte definition through column selection, mobile phase optimization, validation, and final method protocol.

steps.description: Define the target analytes and the sample matrix they sit in.

inputs.name: sample-description
inputs.desc: Description of the sample and its origin

inputs.name: target-analytes
inputs.desc: List of compounds to separate and quantify

inputs.name: required-sensitivity
inputs.desc: Detection limits needed for each analyte

outputs.name: analyte-profile
outputs.desc: Physicochemical properties of each analyte (pKa, logP, MW)

outputs.name: matrix-characterization
outputs.desc: Matrix components that may interfere with separation

outputs.name: method-requirements
outputs.desc: Performance criteria the method must meet

process: List all target analytes with their molecular weights, pKa values, and partition coefficients
Characterize the sample matrix for potential interferents (salts, proteins, lipids)
Define the required sensitivity, resolution, and throughput for the final method
Identify any regulatory or pharmacopeial requirements that apply

steps.description: Select the stationary phase and column dimensions based on analyte properties.

inputs.name: method-requirements
inputs.desc: Performance criteria the method must meet

outputs.name: column-selection
outputs.desc: Chosen column type, particle size, dimensions, and rationale

outputs.name: separation-mode
outputs.desc: Chromatographic mode (reversed-phase, HILIC, ion exchange, normal phase)

process: Match analyte polarity and charge state to the appropriate separation mode
Select particle size and column dimensions based on throughput and resolution requirements
Consider column temperature effects on selectivity
Document the rationale for the chosen stationary phase

steps.description: Optimize the mobile phase composition for the best separation of target analytes.

outputs.name: mobile-phase-composition
outputs.desc: Solvents, buffers, pH, and additives for the mobile phase

outputs.name: gradient-program
outputs.desc: Gradient or isocratic conditions with time program

process: Select the organic modifier and aqueous component based on separation mode
Screen buffer systems and pH values to control analyte ionization
Run scouting gradients to map retention behavior across solvent strength
Optimize the gradient slope and hold times for critical pairs

steps.description: Validate the method against standards for linearity, precision, accuracy, and limits of detection.

outputs.name: validation-results
outputs.desc: Linearity, precision, accuracy, LOD, LOQ for each analyte

outputs.name: system-suitability-criteria
outputs.desc: Pass/fail criteria for routine system suitability testing

process: Prepare calibration standards across the expected concentration range
Run replicate injections to assess precision (intra-day and inter-day)
Spike known amounts into blank matrix to determine accuracy and recovery
Determine limits of detection and quantification from signal-to-noise ratios

steps.description: Assess chromatographic resolution, peak shape, and separation quality.

outputs.name: resolution-report
outputs.desc: Resolution values for critical pairs, peak symmetry, and plate count

outputs.name: method-adjustments
outputs.desc: Any final adjustments to improve peak shape or resolution

process: Calculate resolution between all critical analyte pairs
Measure peak asymmetry factors and theoretical plate counts
Identify any co-elution or shouldering that needs further optimization
Document final adjustments to temperature, flow rate, or gradient

steps.description: Compile the finalized method into a standard operating protocol.

outputs.name: method-protocol
outputs.desc: Complete method protocol ready for routine use

outputs.name: troubleshooting-guide
outputs.desc: Common issues and corrective actions for the method

process: Write the step-by-step method with all instrument parameters
Include sample preparation, injection sequence, and data processing instructions
Attach the validation summary with acceptance criteria
Add a troubleshooting section for retention time drift, pressure changes, and peak shape degradation

description: Model a species' environmental niche from occurrence records through predictor selection, algorithm training, evaluation, projection, and uncertainty assessment.

steps.description: Compile and clean species occurrence records from databases and field surveys.

inputs.name: species-name
inputs.desc: Taxonomic name of the target species

inputs.name: study-extent
inputs.desc: Geographic and temporal bounds for the analysis

inputs.name: data-sources
inputs.desc: Databases and collections to query (GBIF, iNaturalist, museum records)

outputs.name: clean-occurrences
outputs.desc: Georeferenced occurrence records after quality filtering

outputs.name: sampling-bias-assessment
outputs.desc: Description of spatial and temporal biases in the data

process: Query each data source for records within the study extent
Remove duplicates, records with coordinate uncertainty above threshold, and flagged records
Thin points spatially to reduce sampling bias (one record per grid cell)
Document the filtering steps and number of records retained at each stage

steps.description: Select and prepare environmental predictor layers for the niche model.

outputs.name: predictor-stack
outputs.desc: Set of environmental raster layers aligned and clipped to the study extent

outputs.name: collinearity-report
outputs.desc: Pairwise correlations and VIF values, with variables removed if collinear

process: Assemble candidate environmental layers (climate, topography, land cover, soil)
Clip and resample all layers to a common resolution and extent
Compute pairwise correlations and variance inflation factors
Remove collinear variables, retaining those with the strongest ecological rationale

steps.description: Train the niche model using the selected algorithm and occurrence data.

outputs.name: trained-model
outputs.desc: Fitted niche model object or parameter set

outputs.name: variable-importance
outputs.desc: Ranked contribution of each predictor to the model

process: Generate background or pseudo-absence points using an appropriate strategy
Partition the data for cross-validation (spatial blocks to avoid spatial autocorrelation)
Fit the model (MaxEnt, BRT, or random forest) with tuned hyperparameters
Extract variable importance scores and partial response curves

steps.description: Evaluate model performance using discrimination and calibration metrics.

outputs.name: evaluation-metrics
outputs.desc: AUC, TSS, Boyce index, and calibration statistics

outputs.name: threshold-selection
outputs.desc: Binary threshold chosen and its justification

process: Compute AUC and TSS from cross-validation predictions
Assess calibration with the continuous Boyce index
Select the binary threshold (maximum TSS, equal sensitivity-specificity, or fixed sensitivity)
Compare performance across cross-validation folds to assess stability

steps.description: Project the model to new geographic areas or future climate scenarios.

inputs.name: predictor-stack
inputs.desc: Environmental layers for the projection scenario

outputs.name: suitability-map
outputs.desc: Continuous habitat suitability surface

outputs.name: binary-range-map
outputs.desc: Predicted presence/absence map at the chosen threshold

process: Apply the model to the target environmental layers
Flag areas of extrapolation where predictor values fall outside the training range (MESS map)
Apply the binary threshold to produce the range map
Overlay with known range boundaries or protected areas for context

steps.description: Quantify and communicate uncertainty in the niche model predictions.

outputs.name: uncertainty-map
outputs.desc: Spatial map of prediction uncertainty (standard deviation or range across replicates)

outputs.name: niche-model-report
outputs.desc: Final report including methods, results, uncertainty, and recommendations

process: Run bootstrap or ensemble replicates to quantify prediction variance
Map the standard deviation or coefficient of variation across replicates
Identify regions where predictions are least certain
Compile the full report with methods, evaluation, projections, and uncertainty assessment

description: Screen crystallization conditions for a macromolecule or small molecule from sample preparation through screening, optimization, diffraction, and crystal quality assessment.

steps.description: Prepare the sample at the target concentration and purity for crystallization.

inputs.name: purified-sample
inputs.desc: Purified protein or compound with purity assessment

outputs.name: concentrated-sample
outputs.desc: Sample at target concentration with buffer conditions documented

outputs.name: sample-quality-report
outputs.desc: DLS, SDS-PAGE, or other quality metrics confirming monodispersity

process: Concentrate the sample by ultrafiltration to the target range
Measure concentration by UV absorbance or Bradford assay
Assess monodispersity by dynamic light scattering
Document buffer composition, pH, and any additives present

steps.description: Set up the initial crystallization screen matrix using vapor diffusion or batch methods.

inputs.name: screen-selection
inputs.desc: Commercial or custom screen kits to use

outputs.name: screen-plates
outputs.desc: Set of crystallization plates with documented conditions per well

outputs.name: setup-log
outputs.desc: Date, volumes, temperature, and method for each plate

process: Select the screening format (sitting drop, hanging drop, or microbatch under oil)
Dispense reservoir solutions and protein drops using a robot or manually
Seal plates and place at the target temperature (4C or 20C or both)
Record setup date, drop ratios, and reservoir volumes for each condition

steps.description: Image crystallization plates on schedule and score each drop for crystal hits.

outputs.name: imaging-log
outputs.desc: Time-course images of each well

outputs.name: hit-list
outputs.desc: Conditions scored as hits, with crystal morphology and size notes

process: Image plates at scheduled intervals (day 1, 3, 7, 14, 30)
Score each drop using a standard scale (clear, precipitate, microcrystals, single crystals)
Photograph promising hits at higher magnification
Compile the hit list with condition details and crystal descriptions

steps.description: Optimize crystallization conditions around the best hits.

inputs.name: hit-list
inputs.desc: Initial hit conditions to optimize around

outputs.name: optimized-conditions
outputs.desc: Fine-screened conditions that produce the largest, best-shaped crystals

outputs.name: optimization-grid
outputs.desc: pH, precipitant concentration, and additive variations tested

process: Design a grid screen around each hit varying pH, precipitant concentration, and drop ratio
Test additives (salts, small molecules, detergents) for crystal improvement
Set up seeding experiments if nucleation is the bottleneck
Select the conditions producing the largest single crystals with good morphology

steps.description: Harvest crystals and collect X-ray diffraction data.

outputs.name: diffraction-dataset
outputs.desc: Indexed diffraction images with processing statistics

outputs.name: data-collection-log
outputs.desc: Beamline, wavelength, oscillation, exposure, and cryoprotectant details

process: Harvest crystals into cryoprotectant solution and flash-cool in liquid nitrogen
Mount on the beamline and screen for diffraction quality
Collect a complete dataset with appropriate oscillation range and redundancy
Process images to extract intensities and determine the space group and unit cell

steps.description: Assess crystal and diffraction data quality for structure determination suitability.

outputs.name: quality-assessment
outputs.desc: Resolution, completeness, Rmerge, I/sigma, mosaicity, and Wilson B-factor

outputs.name: crystal-screening-report
outputs.desc: Full report from initial screening through data quality, with recommendations

process: Evaluate resolution limits using CC1/2 and I/sigma criteria
Check completeness, redundancy, and Rmerge across resolution shells
Assess mosaicity and ice ring contamination
Compile the full screening report with recommendations for structure determination or further optimization

description: Analyze flow cytometry data from FCS file import through compensation, gating, population statistics, cross-sample comparison, and visualization.

steps.description: Import and parse FCS files into a structured dataset for analysis.

inputs.name: fcs-files
inputs.desc: Raw FCS files from the cytometer

inputs.name: panel-definition
inputs.desc: Antibody panel with fluorochrome assignments and channels

outputs.name: parsed-events
outputs.desc: Event-level data matrix with channel names and metadata

outputs.name: acquisition-summary
outputs.desc: Event count, acquisition time, and instrument settings per file

process: Read the FCS file headers to extract parameter names and metadata
Parse the event data into a matrix of channels by events
Apply any necessary transformations (biexponential, logicle, arcsinh)
Summarize acquisition statistics for each sample

steps.description: Compensate for spectral overlap between fluorochromes using single-stain controls.

outputs.name: compensated-events
outputs.desc: Event data after compensation matrix application

outputs.name: compensation-matrix
outputs.desc: Spillover matrix used, with QC metrics

process: Calculate the spillover matrix from single-stain control samples
Invert the spillover matrix to produce the compensation matrix
Apply the compensation matrix to all event data
Verify compensation by checking that negative populations center at zero on each channel

steps.description: Gate cell populations using sequential bivariate plots or automated clustering.

outputs.name: gated-populations
outputs.desc: Named cell populations with parent-child hierarchy

outputs.name: gating-report
outputs.desc: Gating tree diagram and gate coordinates for reproducibility

process: Apply a scatter gate to exclude debris, doublets, and dead cells
Gate sequentially on lineage markers following the defined hierarchy
For automated gating, run FlowSOM or similar clustering and map clusters to populations
Export the gating tree with coordinates for each gate

steps.description: Extract population frequencies, MFIs, and other summary statistics from gated data.

outputs.name: population-statistics
outputs.desc: Frequencies, absolute counts, MFI, and CV for each population per sample

outputs.name: statistics-table
outputs.desc: Tabular summary ready for downstream statistical testing

process: Compute the percentage of parent for each gated population
Calculate median fluorescence intensity for relevant markers
If bead-based counting was used, convert percentages to absolute counts
Assemble the summary table across all samples and populations

steps.description: Compare population statistics across experimental groups.

outputs.name: comparison-results
outputs.desc: Statistical test results (p-values, effect sizes) for group comparisons

outputs.name: significant-differences
outputs.desc: Populations and markers with statistically significant differences

process: Assign samples to groups according to the experimental design
Select the appropriate statistical test (t-test, ANOVA, Mann-Whitney) based on distribution and sample size
Correct for multiple comparisons (Bonferroni or Benjamini-Hochberg)
Flag populations and markers with significant differences

steps.description: Produce publication-quality visualizations including dimensionality reduction overlays.

inputs.name: compensated-events
inputs.desc: Compensated event data for dimensionality reduction

outputs.name: visualization-panel
outputs.desc: tSNE/UMAP plots, histograms, box plots, and heatmaps

outputs.name: cytometry-report
outputs.desc: Full analysis report with methods, statistics, and figures

process: Downsample events and run tSNE or UMAP for the overview visualization
Color by population or marker expression to show structure
Generate box plots or violin plots for population comparisons with significance annotations
Compile the full analysis report with methods, gating strategy, and figures

description: Analyze electrophysiology recordings from raw trace import through filtering, event detection, feature extraction, classification, and statistical comparison.

steps.description: Import raw electrophysiology traces and associated metadata.

inputs.name: recording-files
inputs.desc: Raw recording files (ABF, NWB, EDF, or proprietary format)

inputs.name: recording-metadata
inputs.desc: Electrode configuration, sampling rate, and recording conditions

outputs.name: raw-traces
outputs.desc: Time-voltage traces for each channel

outputs.name: recording-catalog
outputs.desc: Summary of channels, durations, and protocols per file

process: Read the recording file format and extract voltage traces per channel
Parse protocol information (stimulus type, amplitude, duration, inter-sweep interval)
Verify sampling rate and channel assignments match the expected configuration
Catalog all recordings with their protocols and conditions

steps.description: Filter recordings and reject artifacts to isolate the signal of interest.

inputs.name: recording-metadata
inputs.desc: Sampling rate and expected signal bandwidth

outputs.name: filtered-traces
outputs.desc: Bandpass-filtered traces with artifacts removed

outputs.name: artifact-log
outputs.desc: Timestamps and channels where artifacts were detected and removed

process: Apply a bandpass filter appropriate to the signal type (e.g., 300-3000 Hz for spikes, 1-100 Hz for LFP)
Detect and mark stimulus artifacts, saturation events, and movement artifacts
Blank or interpolate artifact regions
Document filter settings and artifact rejection criteria

steps.description: Detect neural events (spikes, synaptic potentials, oscillations) in filtered traces.

inputs.name: detection-parameters
inputs.desc: Threshold, template, or other detection settings

outputs.name: detected-events
outputs.desc: Timestamps and waveform snippets for each detected event

outputs.name: detection-summary
outputs.desc: Event counts, firing rates, and inter-event interval distributions

process: Set the detection threshold (absolute voltage, RMS multiple, or template match score)
Scan the trace and extract event timestamps and surrounding waveform snippets
Reject false positives by waveform shape or refractory period violation
Compute event rates and inter-event interval distributions

steps.description: Extract quantitative features from detected neural events.

outputs.name: event-features
outputs.desc: Amplitude, half-width, rise time, decay time, and area for each event

outputs.name: feature-summary
outputs.desc: Descriptive statistics of features across all events

process: Measure peak amplitude and trough amplitude for each event
Compute half-width, 10-90% rise time, and decay time constant
Calculate the area under the curve for each event
Summarize features with mean, median, standard deviation, and distributions

steps.description: Classify cell types or response patterns based on electrophysiological features.

inputs.name: event-features
inputs.desc: Extracted features for each event or cell

outputs.name: cell-classifications
outputs.desc: Each cell or unit assigned to a type based on features

outputs.name: classification-criteria
outputs.desc: Rules or clustering results used for classification

process: Cluster waveforms by principal component analysis of feature vectors
Assign clusters to known cell types based on published criteria
For intracellular recordings, classify by firing pattern (regular spiking, fast spiking, bursting)
Document the classification criteria and any ambiguous cases

steps.description: Run statistical comparisons across experimental conditions or cell types.

outputs.name: statistical-results
outputs.desc: Test statistics, p-values, and effect sizes for each comparison

outputs.name: ephys-analysis-report
outputs.desc: Full analysis report with methods, results, and figures

process: Group data by experimental condition and cell type
Select appropriate tests (paired/unpaired, parametric/non-parametric)
Run the comparisons and correct for multiple testing
Compile the report with representative traces, summary plots, and statistical results

description: Identify compounds by mass spectrometry from spectrum acquisition through calibration, deconvolution, database search, fragmentation confirmation, and reporting.

steps.description: Acquire the mass spectrum of the target sample.

inputs.name: sample-introduction
inputs.desc: Sample preparation and introduction method (direct injection, LC, GC)

inputs.name: instrument-parameters
inputs.desc: Ionization mode, scan range, and resolution settings

outputs.name: raw-spectrum
outputs.desc: Mass-to-charge ratio vs intensity data

outputs.name: acquisition-metadata
outputs.desc: Instrument type, ionization method, and acquisition parameters

process: Introduce the sample using the appropriate inlet (ESI, MALDI, EI, APCI)
Acquire the full-scan mass spectrum across the defined m/z range
Acquire MS/MS spectra for the most intense precursor ions
Save raw data with complete metadata for reprocessing

steps.description: Calibrate the mass axis and process raw spectra for accurate mass assignment.

inputs.name: calibrant-reference
inputs.desc: Known calibrant masses for the instrument

outputs.name: calibrated-spectrum
outputs.desc: Mass spectrum with corrected mass axis

outputs.name: mass-accuracy-report
outputs.desc: RMS mass error and calibration residuals

process: Identify calibrant peaks in the spectrum
Fit the calibration function and correct the mass axis
Compute the RMS mass error and verify it meets the target accuracy
Apply baseline subtraction and noise reduction

steps.description: Deconvolute charge state envelopes to determine true molecular masses.

inputs.name: calibrated-spectrum
inputs.desc: Calibrated mass spectrum with charge state series

outputs.name: deconvoluted-masses
outputs.desc: List of neutral molecular masses and their intensities

outputs.name: charge-state-assignments
outputs.desc: Charge state assignment for each peak in the envelope

process: Identify charge state series by their characteristic spacing (1/z Da)
Assign charge states to each peak in the series
Calculate the neutral mass from each charged species and average
Report the deconvoluted mass with precision estimate

steps.description: Search spectral databases for candidate compound identifications.

inputs.name: acquisition-metadata
inputs.desc: Ionization method and instrument type for database filtering

outputs.name: candidate-matches
outputs.desc: Ranked list of candidate compounds with scores and molecular formulas

outputs.name: search-parameters
outputs.desc: Database, mass tolerance, and filters used

process: Query spectral databases (NIST, MassBank, METLIN, mzCloud) within the mass tolerance
Score matches by isotope pattern fit, retention time prediction, and spectral similarity
Filter candidates by ionization mode compatibility and source organism if known
Rank candidates by composite score

steps.description: Confirm identifications using MS/MS fragmentation patterns.

inputs.name: raw-spectrum
inputs.desc: MS/MS spectra for the precursor ions

outputs.name: confirmed-identifications
outputs.desc: Compounds confirmed by fragmentation match with confidence level

outputs.name: fragment-annotations
outputs.desc: Annotated fragment ions with proposed structures

process: Extract the MS/MS spectrum for each candidate precursor ion
Match observed fragments against the predicted fragmentation pattern
Score the match using a mirror plot comparison and fragment coverage
Assign a confidence level (1: standard match, 2: spectral library, 3: informatic prediction)

steps.description: Compile the identification results into a structured report.

inputs.name: confirmed-identifications
inputs.desc: Confirmed compound identifications with confidence levels

outputs.name: identification-report
outputs.desc: Final report listing identified compounds, evidence level, and spectra

outputs.name: unidentified-features
outputs.desc: Masses that could not be identified, with partial structural information if available

process: Compile all confirmed identifications with their supporting evidence
List unidentified masses with any partial structural information (molecular formula, substructure)
Include annotated spectra for each confirmed compound
State the confidence level and limitations for each identification

description: Date a geological or archaeological sample using radiometric methods from system selection through measurement, correction, age calculation, and quality assessment.

steps.description: Select the appropriate radiometric dating system based on the sample and expected age range.

inputs.name: sample-description
inputs.desc: Mineral type, rock type, or organic material

inputs.name: expected-age-range
inputs.desc: Approximate age range to constrain system choice

inputs.name: available-material
inputs.desc: Amount and condition of sample available

outputs.name: dating-system
outputs.desc: Selected system (14C, K-Ar, Ar-Ar, U-Pb, Rb-Sr, Sm-Nd, Lu-Hf, or other)

outputs.name: system-rationale
outputs.desc: Why this system is appropriate and its limitations for this sample

process: Match the sample type to systems where the parent isotope is present in measurable quantity
Confirm the expected age falls within the effective range of the system
Consider the half-life, closure temperature, and susceptibility to open-system behavior
Document the rationale and flag any potential complications

steps.description: Prepare the sample for isotopic measurement by the selected dating system.

outputs.name: prepared-aliquot
outputs.desc: Sample prepared for mass spectrometry (dissolved, separated, spiked)

outputs.name: preparation-log
outputs.desc: Steps taken, blank levels, spike calibration, and yield

process: Separate the target mineral phase if needed (zircon, sanidine, whole rock)
Dissolve the sample and add isotopic tracer (spike) for concentration measurement
Perform chemical separation to isolate the parent and daughter elements
Measure procedural blanks to assess contamination

steps.description: Measure parent and daughter isotope ratios on the mass spectrometer.

inputs.name: dating-system
inputs.desc: Isotopic system dictating which ratios to measure

outputs.name: measured-ratios
outputs.desc: Isotope ratios with internal precision (2SE)

outputs.name: measurement-conditions
outputs.desc: Instrument type, ion beam intensities, and run parameters

process: Load the sample into the mass spectrometer (TIMS, MC-ICP-MS, or SIMS depending on system)
Measure the isotope ratios with sufficient cycles for the target precision
Monitor fractionation and correct using the exponential law or a standard
Report internal precision as 2 standard errors of the mean

steps.description: Apply corrections for common lead, blank, fractionation, and interference.

outputs.name: corrected-ratios
outputs.desc: Isotope ratios after all corrections

outputs.name: correction-summary
outputs.desc: Magnitude and uncertainty of each correction applied

process: Subtract the procedural blank contribution from each ratio
Correct for common lead using the appropriate model (Stacey-Kramers or measured)
Apply mass fractionation correction if not already done during measurement
Propagate the uncertainty from each correction through to the final ratios

steps.description: Calculate the age from corrected isotope ratios with full uncertainty propagation.

inputs.name: dating-system
inputs.desc: Decay constants and age equation to use

outputs.name: calculated-age
outputs.desc: Age with 2-sigma uncertainty

outputs.name: concordance-assessment
outputs.desc: For U-Pb: concordia age or degree of discordance

process: Apply the appropriate age equation for the dating system
Propagate all sources of uncertainty (analytical, blank, decay constant, common lead model)
For U-Pb, plot on concordia and assess concordance or discordance
For isochron systems, regress the data and assess MSWD

steps.description: Assess whether the sample has remained a closed system since formation.

outputs.name: system-integrity-verdict
outputs.desc: Assessment of closed-system behavior (concordant, discordant, reset, or mixed)

outputs.name: geochronology-report
outputs.desc: Final dating report with age, uncertainty, and geological interpretation

process: Evaluate concordance or isochron fit (MSWD, probability of fit)
Check for evidence of Pb loss, excess Ar, or other open-system indicators
Compare the age with independent constraints (stratigraphy, other dating systems)
Write the final report with the preferred age interpretation and its caveats

description: Characterize enzyme kinetics from assay design through data collection, Michaelis-Menten fitting, inhibition testing, and kinetic parameter reporting.

steps.description: Design the enzyme kinetic assay including substrate range, enzyme concentration, and detection method.

inputs.name: enzyme-info
inputs.desc: Enzyme name, source, purity, and known properties

inputs.name: substrate-info
inputs.desc: Substrate identity, solubility, and approximate Km if known

inputs.name: detection-method
inputs.desc: Spectrophotometric, fluorometric, or coupled assay details

outputs.name: assay-protocol
outputs.desc: Complete assay protocol with concentrations, volumes, and timing

outputs.name: substrate-range
outputs.desc: Substrate concentrations to test (spanning 0.2x to 5x estimated Km)

process: Select the enzyme concentration that gives linear product formation over the measurement window
Define the substrate concentration series spanning well below and above the estimated Km
Set buffer conditions (pH, temperature, cofactors, ionic strength)
Define the detection method and its linear range for the product

steps.description: Collect initial velocity data across the substrate concentration range.

outputs.name: velocity-data
outputs.desc: Initial velocity at each substrate concentration (replicated)

outputs.name: progress-curves
outputs.desc: Full time courses to verify linearity of the initial rate region

process: Run the assay at each substrate concentration in at least triplicate
Record the full progress curve (product vs time) for each reaction
Determine the initial velocity from the linear portion of each progress curve
Flag any substrate concentrations where the progress curve is not linear

steps.description: Fit the Michaelis-Menten equation to the initial velocity data.

inputs.name: velocity-data
inputs.desc: Initial velocity vs substrate concentration data

outputs.name: km-vmax
outputs.desc: Km and Vmax with standard errors from the nonlinear fit

outputs.name: fit-quality
outputs.desc: R-squared, residual plot, and Lineweaver-Burk plot for comparison

process: Fit the hyperbolic Michaelis-Menten equation by nonlinear least-squares regression
Extract Km and Vmax with their standard errors
Inspect the residual plot for systematic deviations (substrate inhibition, cooperativity)
Generate a Lineweaver-Burk (double reciprocal) plot as a visual check

steps.description: Test for inhibition and determine the inhibition type and Ki.

inputs.name: velocity-data
inputs.desc: Initial velocity data with and without inhibitor

outputs.name: inhibition-type
outputs.desc: Classification as competitive, uncompetitive, mixed, or noncompetitive

outputs.name: ki-value
outputs.desc: Inhibition constant with standard error

process: Collect velocity data at multiple inhibitor concentrations across the substrate range
Fit global models for competitive, uncompetitive, and mixed inhibition
Compare models by AIC or F-test to select the best fit
Extract Ki (and Ki' for mixed) with standard errors

steps.description: Compile kinetic parameters into the final analysis report.

outputs.name: kinetics-report
outputs.desc: Full kinetic characterization report with parameters, plots, and interpretation

outputs.name: parameter-table
outputs.desc: Summary table of all kinetic constants with units and uncertainties

process: Compile Km, Vmax, kcat (if enzyme concentration is known), kcat/Km, Ki into a summary table
Include Michaelis-Menten plots, Lineweaver-Burk plots, and Dixon plots
State the assay conditions (buffer, pH, temperature) and their effect on parameter interpretation
Compare parameters against published values if available

description: Analyze genetic variation in a population from genotyping through allele frequency calculation, Hardy-Weinberg testing, diversity metrics, selection detection, and structure inference.

steps.description: Prepare and quality-filter genotype data for population genetic analysis.

inputs.name: raw-genotypes
inputs.desc: Genotype calls from SNP array, sequencing, or microsatellites

inputs.name: sample-metadata
inputs.desc: Population labels, sampling locations, and sample quality metrics

outputs.name: filtered-genotypes
outputs.desc: QC-passed genotype matrix with individuals and loci retained

outputs.name: qc-summary
outputs.desc: Missingness rates, call rates, and samples or loci removed

process: Filter individuals with excessive missing data (above threshold)
Filter loci with low call rate or extreme deviation from Hardy-Weinberg across all populations
Check for and remove related individuals using identity-by-descent estimates
Report the final dataset dimensions and any concerns

steps.description: Calculate allele frequencies and genotype frequencies per population.

outputs.name: allele-frequencies
outputs.desc: Minor allele frequency per locus per population

outputs.name: maf-spectrum
outputs.desc: Site frequency spectrum for each population

process: Count alleles per locus within each population
Compute minor allele frequency and genotype frequencies
Build the site frequency spectrum (folded or unfolded)
Identify fixed differences and private alleles between populations

steps.description: Test each locus for departure from Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium within each population.

outputs.name: hwe-results
outputs.desc: Chi-square or exact test p-values for HWE at each locus per population

outputs.name: hwe-deviations
outputs.desc: Loci showing significant departure from HWE, with excess or deficit of heterozygotes

process: Compute expected genotype frequencies from allele frequencies under HWE
Perform exact tests for HWE at each locus within each population
Correct for multiple testing
Interpret departures (inbreeding, selection, population structure, or genotyping error)

steps.description: Compute diversity and differentiation metrics across populations.

outputs.name: diversity-metrics
outputs.desc: Observed and expected heterozygosity, nucleotide diversity (pi), Watterson's theta

outputs.name: differentiation-metrics
outputs.desc: Pairwise Fst, Gst, and Jost's D between populations

process: Compute observed and expected heterozygosity per population
Calculate nucleotide diversity (pi) and Watterson's theta if sequence data
Compute pairwise Fst between all population pairs (Weir and Cockerham)
Calculate Tajima's D to detect deviations from neutral expectations

steps.description: Scan for signatures of natural selection in the genome.

outputs.name: selection-candidates
outputs.desc: Genomic regions with outlier Fst, extended haplotype homozygosity, or other selection signals

outputs.name: selection-scan-summary
outputs.desc: Methods used, significance thresholds, and number of candidates

process: Scan for Fst outliers across the genome (top 1% or empirical p-value)
Compute extended haplotype homozygosity (EHH/iHS) for recent positive selection if phased data available
Cross-reference outlier regions with annotated genes
Report candidate regions with their gene content and functional annotations

steps.description: Infer population structure and admixture proportions.

outputs.name: structure-results
outputs.desc: Admixture proportions (Q-matrix) at the best K, with cross-validation error

outputs.name: popgen-report
outputs.desc: Full population genetics report with all metrics, structure, and selection results

process: Run PCA to visualize population clustering in genetic space

Apply gross error checks: physical limits, temporal consistency, spatial coherence
Flag suspect values but do not remove them yet
Document data sources, versions, and access dates
